title: Aaron Boone ‘surprised but not surprised’ by Mets firing Carlos Mendoza
content:
BOSTON — Aaron Boone was one of Carlos Mendoza’s biggest proponents before the latter was named the New York Mets’ manager in November 2023. Mendoza worked his way up the New York Yankees’ organization before becoming one of Boone’s closest confidants since he became the club’s manager in 2018.

Even as opposing managers in New York City, the two remained close. When the Mets were struggling earlier this season, Boone was quick to offer advice and be a sounding board. Still, he knew it was possible that Friday’s news would be coming at some point: The Mets, amid a six-game losing streak, fired Mendoza in his third season as manager.

“Surprised, I guess, but not surprised,” Boone said. “Obviously, it’s a tough situation over there right now with what they’ve been through this year, and even going back to last year.”

The Mets have been one of MLB’s biggest disappointments this year. Despite having the second-highest payroll in the league, according to FanGraphs, the Mets are last in the National League East. Run prevention was the club’s strategy heading into 2026, but the Mets have been a disaster in that category. Their starting pitchers have a collective 4.90 ERA, third-worst in MLB. As a club, they’ve also committed the third-most errors, including six in an embarrassing effort on Wednesday.

Boone said he spoke with Mendoza on Friday and said the now-former Mets manager is “in a good place.” He also believes that Mendoza, who finished his tenure with a 206-199 record, will eventually be a manager again.

“He’s really good at what he does,” Boone said. “He’s a great leader that, as time goes on, my expectation is that he’ll be in line for another job in a lot of different ways, shapes, and forms, and he has earned a strong reputation in the industry. I think even through all this, I think it solidified that reputation.”

Boone named Mendoza his bench coach in 2019, and he remained in that role through the 2023 season until the Mets hired him. During his time with the Yankees, Mendoza was known as a disciplinarian behind the scenes, but the team loved and respected his hard coaching. His departure was seen as a considerable loss inside the organization.

Mendoza led the Mets to the National League Championship Series in 2024, but the past two seasons have been failures. The Mets collapsed in the second half of last season to miss the postseason, and they entered Friday night 13 games under .500. That’s why Boone thought one of his closest friends in the business was in jeopardy of losing his job.

“Can I say I’m really surprised that this happened with what they’ve been through?” Boone rhetorically asked. “No, not necessarily. Still, when you hear the news, it catches you (off guard). I think he’s a great baseball man. I think he’s a really good leader, and I think he’s a really good manager that will get another opportunity.”
